articles.headline: Business sample story 1
articles.excerpt: A sample business story — the real edition brings today's world news at three reading levels.

Beginner.text: This is a short, simple sample story. It uses easy words and short sentences. The real edition will have today's world news written just for learners. Tap a level to change the reading.

vocab.definition: new information about events
a business that sells things
what people use to buy things
a person who plays a sport
how much something costs

Intermediate.text: This is a sample article at the intermediate level. It is a little longer and uses clearer, everyday English. When the daily edition runs, each category will have five real news stories from around the world, written at three levels. You can switch levels, learn the vocabulary, and answer the questions at the bottom.

vocab.definition: all the companies in one type of business
how much people want something
a plan or rule made by a government
the money a business earns
to try to win against others
the people who watch or listen

Advanced.text: This is a sample article at the advanced level, and it is noticeably longer, with richer sentences and more challenging vocabulary. Once the automated build runs each morning, The Daily Scoop will gather current world news across six categories and rewrite every story at three carefully graded levels. Advanced readers get more detail, more nuanced language, and a longer passage, while the vocabulary list highlights harder, more academic words to expand your range. Use the level switch, the Fast Reading button, and the comprehension questions to study at your own pace.

vocab.definition: the tendency to change quickly and unpredictably
a person or group with an interest in something
the basic systems a country or organization needs to work
the ability to recover quickly from difficulty
an estimate of a future amount based on current data
to combine several things into one stronger whole
never having happened before

questions.q: What is this website for?
questions.a: Reading world news in English at different levels.

questions.q: How many reading levels are there?
questions.a: Three (Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced).
